articles.body: Erin Ogunkeye welcomes Reed Brody, Member of the International Commission of Jurists, Human Rights Lawyer and veteran war crimes prosecutor. The International Court of Justice's ruling on Myanmar marks, according to Brody, "a historic victory for the Rohingya, but also a landmark for international justice." He explains how the court assessed evidence of genocidal intent, rejecting Myanmar's justification of its military operations as counterterrorism. He argues that "the existence of an armed conflict or a security objective doesn't exclude genocidal intent," a finding he believes will have "far-reaching implications in future genocide cases," including South Africa's case against Israel over Gaza. articles.body: Iowa Gov.-elect Rob Sand isn’t indulging any consideration of him as a potential 2028 presidential candidate. Sand, who cemented himself as a rising star in the party by flipping the governor’s seat in Iowa with a commanding 11-point victory, said in an onstage interview at the POLITICO Pub on the sidelines of the National Governors Association’s New Governors Leadership Forum that he’s unlikely to ever consider running for president. “Are you completely taking 2028 off the table?” POLITICO’s Adam Wren asked Sand. “Yes,” he replied. When asked if he would ever consider running for president, Sand curtly replied, “Doubt it.” Sand offered a tongue-in-cheek rebuttal to the suggestion that he could position himself as an influential voice and a power broker in the national conversation ahead of the next election. “Ooh, that sounds exciting,” Sand quipped sarcastically before adding, “I expect to be a governor in 2027 and in 2028.” Sand also declined to weigh in on his preference for who Democrats should nominate in the presidential primaries. Asked to choose between Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear, Arizona Sen. Mark Kelly and former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg — all of whom campaigned for Democrats in Iowa in the midterms — Sand refused to take the bait. “We have forever to go on all of this,” he said. “The people who want to do that, they're going to get in the race. They're going to do things. They're going to say things. We'll learn a lot more. Then we'll have a clear opinion about who should be doing what.” Sand reiterated that he intends to keep Iowa’s Democratic caucuses as the first nominating contest on the calendar despite the Democratic Party removing Iowa from its early state lineup and encouraged Democratic presidential candidates to continue the tradition of visiting Iowa’s state fair next year. “I'm pretty confident that we'll figure something out that means we're following Iowa law, and they're going to be able to do that,” he said.
articles.headline: Rob Sand shuts down any talk of 2028

articles.body: Democrats want fighters. Massachusetts Gov. Maura Healey believes they want healers, too. Healey, a Democrat who easily won a second term in the deep-blue state earlier this month, told POLITICO on Thursday that she’d like to see her party’s next presidential nominee show “decency” and “humanity.” “It’s really important that we have leaders who genuinely see people, understand their situation. If you don't see people, if you don't understand people, you're never going to be able to deliver for them,” Healey said during an interview at the POLITICO Pub on the sidelines of the National Governors Association’s New Governors Leadership Forum in Deer Valley, Utah. “Having leaders who have that, and who have a strong moral compass, I think that's really important,” she told POLITICO’s Adam Wren. Healey suggested the midterms offered a “resetting” as the nation moves toward a post-Donald Trump era. Pressed on whether it’s more important for Democrats to nominate a fighter or a healer, Healey — who burnished her national profile as a hard-charging state attorney general who sued the first Trump administration dozens of times and urged Democrats to more aggressively oppose his second — insisted good leaders can do both. “You can be a uniter and a fighter; you can be a fighter and a healer,” she said. It’s a debate that’s already driving the earliest stages of Democrats’ shadow 2028 primary as the party’s rising stars try to discern whether voters who powered their midterm wave want a brawler or a uniter after candidates of both stripes won difficult races. Healey ruled out a 2028 presidential bid of her own on Thursday. And she deflected when asked whether Democrats should nominate a governor. But the Massachusetts governor, who has close relationships with several likely contenders and routinely hits the campaign trail for Democrats in the early primary state of New Hampshire, could play a role in shaping the primary.
articles.headline: Massachusetts gov says Dems want ‘a uniter and a fighter’ for 2028

articles.body: Georgia Democratic Gov.-elect Keisha Lance Bottoms said the midterm election results “have spoken for themselves” in showing the need for the Democratic Party to invest more in the South. “I would hope that in two years, we're not having to beg and borrow to be able to run successful campaigns,” Bottoms said in an onstage interview at the POLITICO Pub on the sidelines of the National Governors Association’s New Governors Leadership Forum in Utah. Democrats had a historically strong cycle in Georgia this year: Bottoms became the first Democrat to win her state’s governorship in more than a quarter-century, Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff won reelection handily, and the party flipped the state House for the first time in more than two decades. But it wasn’t just Georgia. Democrats also won Senate seats in North Carolina, South Carolina and Mississippi, three states that have long been out of reach for the party, and just missed in Louisiana. “The numbers have been there for Democrats to flip that seat in Mississippi for a while, but the investment has not been there,” Bottoms said. She said that her campaign was a lean operation, particularly in contrast to her GOP opponent’s. Rick Jackson spent nearly $200 million of his own money on his campaign. “During the primary it was the shoestring, dental floss campaign, we were holding it together with every single thing that we had because we weren't getting in the resources and some people have written Georgia off,” she said. “But also even when those resources come from our friends nationally: Trust us. Nobody knows their community, nobody knows their electorate better than the people who are living and breathing it every single day.” Bottoms made history as the first-ever Black woman ever elected governor to in the U.S. earlier this month. But on her campaign trail, she did not focus on the historic nature of her candidacy. “I wake up as a Black woman every day,” she said. “So it was not something that I felt compelled to talk about, it was never top of mind, so it was not even a conscious decision for me not to talk about it. I just didn’t think about it.” She said she instead focused on voters’ cost of living concerns that dominated the cycle. “For me, it was about focusing on the issues. I can't hide, and don't want to hide, that I'm a Black woman,” she said. “To the extent that the conversations were organic with me as a mother or as a woman or whatever the case may have been, then it was a part of the discussion. But I can tell you, as I moved around the state of Georgia, people were focused on, ‘what are you gonna do about this cost of living? How are you going to make my life better?’”
articles.headline: Keisha Lance Bottoms says Democrats better spend big on the South

articles.body: Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear defended his decision not to invest more in Gina Hinojosa’s successful race for Texas governor in an interview with POLITICO, amid criticism that could derail his own potential presidential ambitions. Beshear, the chair of the Democratic Governors Association, took heat this month when Latino Democratic operatives and Hinojosa allies publicly maligned him for failing to do enough to help Hinojosa over the finish line. “There might have been frustration by folks who just really wanted to win that race, but they did, and she did, and we're very excited to have her a part of the DGA room,” Beshear said Thursday. “Did we spend a little more money, say, in Kansas, where we were trying to protect the seat? Yes, but we only won that race by 7,000 votes," he said. In a stunning victory, Hinojosa won Texas by 7 percentage points. Hinojosa’s allies’ say that their calls for the DGA to support her campaign went unanswered for months. Ultimately, the DGA contributed $1.4 million — a far cry from the $19 million the organization invested in Keisha Lance Bottoms’ successful bid to win Georgia’s governorship. But Beshear said the context matters. When the budget for this campaign cycle started at the end of 2024, Democrats had suffered brutal losses. “We built out our map protecting our incumbents,” Beshear said. “We were going to be lucky to get [Arizona Gov.] Katie Hobbs and [Oregon Gov.] Tina Kotek reelected, and we were going to have tough elections, even in places potentially like Pennsylvania.” Democrats Abigail Spanberger in Virginia and Mikie Sherrill in New Jersey both won gubernatorial victories in 2025 on affordability platforms, which helped propel them to victory at a time when the economy had become a key pressure point for voters. Heading into 2026, Beshear said, "what came online were the first set of flips, where the earliest polling indicated it was possible, and those were Iowa, Ohio, Georgia and Nevada. And so at that point, we already had the largest DGA map ever." “We had a size 10 budget with a size 14 map, and then what happened? Alaska, Nebraska, Oklahoma, Texas and Florida all became or seemed competitive as well, which meant we had a size 10 budget with a size 16 map," Beshear said. The party flipped six governorships in states that President Donald Trump won. In January, Democrats will control 30 governorships and the majority of state legislative chambers. “So at the end of the day, I think we're judged by results,” Beshear said. “And I get that every campaign wants as much funding as they can, but Gina won in Texas, and I'm excited for her.” While Beshear hasn’t publicly announced a run for president in 2028, he’s already crafting his pitch. “If you look at what we've done in Kentucky, the ability to do that all across this country would be special for so many other communities that deserve better jobs, more accessible health care and a better life for our people,” he said. Despite his role as chair of the DGA, Beshear argues that of all the rumored candidates out there, he would be the “ultimate outsider.” He’s not from “inside the Beltway” or either coast. He would be “a candidate from where the South meets the Midwest,” he said — a governor who has helped “improve and revive a place that the country for many years left out.” Beshear says that Bottoms’ victory in Georgia showed Democrats can win in the South. “I am a Southern governor that has won in a red state, and so I knew a great candidate when I saw one,” he said. “And together, our financial support plus her grassroots campaign that turned out voters sent a message that the South is winnable and that the Deep South is winnable.” Next up? Mississippi and Louisiana, Beshear said. “You look at Mississippi, where three years ago the election was close and will be again,” he said. “And then, depending on the candidate we get in Louisiana, the governor there has incredibly low approval ratings, and so even though that's going up against an incumbent, I think the seat is very much in play.” In 2023, Mississippi Gov. Tate Reeves defeated his Democratic nominee Brandon Presley by 3.24 percentage points. Louisiana Gov. Jeff Landry took office in January 2024.
articles.headline: Beshear defends Texas strategy

articles.body: CHICAGO — The head of the Democratic Attorneys General Association is stepping down after a successful 2026 cycle in which their party flipped Republican-held attorney general offices in five states, including the conservative legal powerhouse of Texas. Sean Rankin started as executive director at the group — known as DAGA — in 2016, and oversaw its operations as Democratic attorneys general banded together to challenge the first Trump administration over a range of issues. He became president of the group in 2022 and is credited with raising nearly $250 million for DAGA and its affiliated entities over the past decade. “Since Sean joined DAGA in 2016, the committee has won the majority of their competitive races” against Republicans, “reshaping the map for Democrats,” the group said Thursday. Rankin will stay at DAGA as it conducts a search for his successor. Democrats will take control of at least five additional attorney general offices in January, following wins in Texas, Georgia, Ohio, Kansas and Iowa. Alaska, which just elected a Democratic governor, is also expected to have a Democratic attorney general, since the governor appoints the state's top lawyer. “On Texas, we took the head of the snake. So fundamentally, there will be a change in how the Republican attorneys general have to engage nationally if they do not have Texas at the front,” Rankin told POLITICO in a wide-ranging interview after the midterms earlier this month. “Texas has played an outsized role in the actions taken, in my opinion, against many of the issues that I care about, that the AGs fight for, that we believe the American people support — having Texas not on the other side, that’s a game changer.”

articles.body: North Carolina Gov. Josh Stein said his state needs to roll back subsidies for data centers, telling POLITICO that Big Tech companies should be “paying their own way.” “I think the idea that this industry needs any public incentive is laughable. These are the wealthiest companies in the history of humanity. They have more resources than many nations. So we, little North Carolina, should not be giving subsidies,” Stein said in an interview Thursday at the POLITICO Pub at the National Governors Association’s New Governors Leadership Forum in Deer Valley, Utah. The Democratic governor pointed to subsidies in North Carolina for electricity for data centers that were rolled back earlier this year , along with ongoing subsidies for the purchase of new equipment, which he said ought to be phased out. “For new data centers, why are we giving them any public dollar when they should be subsidizing the ratepayers?” he said. Stein, elected in 2024, will be governing with a divided Legislature next year after Democrats flipped North Carolina’s House of Representatives this year and broke the Republican supermajority in the state Senate amid a nationwide blue wave . Republicans are likely to maintain narrow control of the upper chamber pending a recount in a pivotal race. The first-term governor, who won by nearly 15 points in 2024 despite President Donald Trump also winning the state that year, didn’t commit to running again in 2028 but said he “cannot think of any” reasons not to. Stein touted bipartisan work in the state to address recovery from Hurricane Helene, which devastated western North Carolina in 2024. But he faulted “one of the most ineffectual Congresses in history” for failing to deliver for the state. The $60 billion in damages North Carolina suffered, he noted, are nearly as large of a sum as the state’s two-year budget — making it impossible for the state to allocate enough funds for recovery. He said that he spoke to Trump earlier this year and was told that hurricane recovery was a priority for the president, but the necessary federal funds have not come through. “The state stepped up,” Stein said. “The people of Western North Carolina have truly stepped up, and it's time for the federal government to step up.”
articles.headline: ‘They should be subsidizing the ratepayers’: NC governor says data center subsidies should be rolled back

articles.body: Nevada Democratic Gov.-elect Aaron Ford is vowing to immediately pass a trifecta of measures that he says will drive down the cost of living when he enters office in the key swing state. “Those are concrete things that immediately can bring some level of effect to this cost-of-living crisis that we're experiencing right now,” Ford told POLITICO’s Megan Messerly in an onstage interview at the National Governors Association’s New Governors Leadership Forum in Utah. The legislative blitz includes a bill to make school breakfast and lunch free for public school students, legislation that would limit the cost of prescription drugs to the Medicare-negotiated price for everybody and new rules aimed at lowering housing costs that would limit the number of homes corporations can purchase. “I've been working with my colleagues already in the Legislature, and we're going to sign bills beginning on Day 1,” Ford said. “We'll be signing bills within the first 30 days to ensure that we can start effectuating some of the promises that I made on the campaign trail. “You hear people signing executive orders to make things easier for businesses — cut regulations and make it easier to do business — I think that’s cool, that’s fine, and that’s dandy. But if you could do it for businesses, you could do it for people too,” he also said. The incoming Nevada governor and former state attorney general also emphasized his willingness to work across the aisle — even though the massive Democratic wins in his state earlier this month make it so “I don't need one Republican vote to get something done in my state right now,” he said. Nevada will be the second state to vote in the Democratic primaries in 2028, and Ford said candidates need to come and travel up and down the state before staking out policy positions. “You need to come to Nevada. Period. Point blank,” Ford said. “We’re one of the most diverse states in the nation. If you can convince a Nevadan that you’re worth your salt, you may very well be able to convince the rest of the nation that you are.” And he cautioned Democrats against making assumptions on what Nevadans want and need. “Don’t presume you know what their issues are,” he said. “Don’t be high and mighty and highfalutin and sitting in some ivory tower putting out ideas when you haven’t heard them say to you what their concerns are.”
articles.headline: Nevada's new governor promises legislative blitz on affordability

articles.body: Vice President JD Vance took aim at Kevin Stitt, calling the Republican governor of Oklahoma’s push for bipartisan immigration reform “morally and electorally disastrous.” “I like Kevin, but what does ‘bipartisan immigration reform’ mean?” Vance wrote on X on Thursday morning. “If you mean making it harder for megacompanies to defraud our visa system, great. If you mean we should pass legislation to make it harder for employers to violate our immigration law, I'm all ears,” Vance wrote. “But to a lot of people, this sounds like an effort to give amnesty to people who have broken our laws. It is morally and electorally disastrous.” The vice president was responding to comments the Oklahoma Republican made at the POLITICO Pub on the sidelines of the National Governors Association’s New Governors Leadership Forum in Park City, Utah, on Wednesday. “We need to have a strong border. We need to know who is coming into our country. We need to vet those people,” Stitt said. Stitt described President Donald Trump as a “businessperson” who “understands the need for a workforce.” “He can lead on this, he can fix this immigration policy,” the Oklahoma governor said. But he blamed Congress and other interests in Washington for standing in the way of reform. “It’s not that complicated. But the problem is Washington, D.C., each side thinks they’re winning on it. They raise money off of it. They politic off of it. They try to crush the other side over these issues instead of fixing it for the American people,” Stitt said. “That’s why you saw this huge swing in the midterms.” Asked about Vance’s comments on Thursday, Stitt told POLITICO he was “super pumped that the vice president is being engaged in the conversations.” “The governors have been leading on this,” Stitt added. “Republican governors, Democrat governors, have a lot to say on immigration policy, and I am glad the vice president is listening.” Stitt has long called for sweeping changes to immigration policy, including enabling state governors to issue work permits to unauthorized immigrants. Vance – who is weighing a run for the White House in 2028 – has been a staunch defender of the Trump administration’s aggressive crackdown on illegal immigration. Trump has signaled he is open to cutting a deal on immigration reform in the wake of his party’s midterm defeats. The president told CBS News’s “60 Minutes” earlier this month that his deportation policy was “ too tough ” and had hurt Republicans with some midterm voters. But any agreement still seems unlikely. The same day he spoke to “60 Minutes,” Trump named immigration hardliner Stephen Miller to be White House chief of staff. Asked about the possibility of a deal earlier this week, Trump told reporters at the White House: “It would be wonderful, but we’ll see.” The president said any agreement would “have to be tough” and offer “no amnesty” for unauthorized immigrants.
articles.headline: JD Vance slams GOP governor’s call for immigration reform as ‘morally and electorally disastrous’

articles.body: Allies of former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg are launching an independent, grassroots effort urging him to undertake a second presidential campaign ahead of 2028. Team Pete PAC will be led by Jennifer Holdsworth, the former national campaign manager of Buttigieg’s unsuccessful 2017 bid for DNC chair, and Mohsin Syed, his former chief of staff at the Transportation Department. The PAC is aiming to bring together volunteers and grassroots donors who backed Buttigieg’s 2020 presidential bid. “Mohsin and I have traveled the country this year, and everywhere we go, people ask us the same question: how can I help Pete?” Holdsworth said in a statement. Team Pete PAC is independent and has no ties to Buttigieg’s Win the Era PAC, nor is it a presidential committee. Through Win the Era, Buttigieg campaigned with 102 candidates across the map for the midterms, visiting 38 states (19 of them twice). Asked on MS NOW’s “Morning Joe” on Wednesday whether he had a timeline to make a decision, Buttigieg said he would be “surprised” if he was the first potential 2028 presidential candidate “to make news” and said he’s “certainly not cooking up anything to announce in the next few weeks.” Even as it forms to press Buttigieg to mount a second presidential campaign, Team Pete PAC is urging potential backers to take part in community service — a nod to Buttigeig’s proposed national service program he proposed as a candidate. “I’ve seen up close what Pete can do,” Syed said. “He has a unique ability to bring people together and inspire action.”
articles.headline: Buttigieg allies launch effort to back another presidential run

articles.body: Utah’s Republican governor wants his party to move beyond President Donald Trump heading into the next presidential election. “It’s time for the next thing,” Gov. Spencer Cox said in an interview on Wednesday at the POLITICO Pub, on the sidelines of the National Governors Association’s New Governors Leadership Forum in Deer Valley, Utah. Cox called on his fellow Republicans to start looking for new leadership in the wake of this month’s midterm election defeats. “This is how this works when presidents move on. We should be looking for the next leadership in our party and what that looks like,” Cox told POLITICO’s Samuel Benson. “We’ve got JD Vance and Marco Rubio, and those seem to be kind of the two choices now,” Cox said, referring to the Vice President and Secretary of State, respectively. “But I think you’ll see a lot of people step up … there are a lot of really interesting folks.” “I’m a fan of governors,” Cox added. “I think governors with executive experience are the best to lead the country.” Vance told Fox News earlier this week that he would decide “sometime next year” whether he will run for president in 2028. Rubio has dismissed suggestions that he would launch his own bid, and has said he would support Vance if the Vice President ran for the White House. “I am hopeful that there are some Republican governors that will throw their hat in,” said Cox, a two-term governor. “We can have a competition of ideas heading in to find out what's next.” Cox said that Trump still has a “really important role to play” in leading the party over the next two years, adding that the president still had an “opportunity” to strike bipartisan deals on permitting reform and other policy areas in his last two years in office. Cox called the president “unique,” adding: “He’s someone who has the attention of the country in a way that almost no president has had in my lifetime.” “People really love him or really don’t like him, but everybody’s paying attention to him,” he said.
articles.headline: Utah GOP governor on Trump and 2028: ‘It’s time for the next thing’

articles.body: Deb Haaland is about to take the helm of a newly-minted Democratic presidential primary battleground. She has thoughts for her party’s White House hopefuls on how to win there. Haaland, New Mexico’s incoming governor, told POLITICO that immigration will be a “top issue” in the presidential election — one that she’s “anxious” to see how future candidates plan to address — and said that engaging with rural voters in her state will be key to any successful primary campaign. “New Mexico is the fifth largest state, and we are largely rural,” Haaland told POLITICO’s Erin Doherty in an onstage interview at the National Governors Association's New Governors Leadership Forum in Utah. “There are far more rural communities than there are large cities in our state, and so this will be important for New Mexicans to to really understand or to really know that any presidential candidate understands the challenges that they're facing.” Immigration is “going to be a top issue with the 2028 presidential election,” she added. “New Mexico is an early primary state, and it happens that we're a border state, too.” Haaland’s ascension to the governor’s mansion coincides with a major change in New Mexico’s place in the Democratic Party's presidential nominating calendar pecking order. The state will now be fourth in the voting calendar behind South Carolina, Nevada and New Hampshire. The move gives New Mexicans — and their new governor — significant influence in shaping the kind of nominee the party selects to take back the White House. It’ll also pose a significant test for candidate’s engagement with Latino voters, as New Mexico ranks first nationwide in its population share of Latino residents. Some of those potential candidates have already come calling. “Rahm Emanuel was in New Mexico, and he did quite a bit of traveling around,” Haaland said, noting that several senators made their own sojourns to the state for an event hosted in October by Democratic Sen. Ben Ray Luján in Alberquerque. Former Secretary of Transportation Pete Buttigieg made his own trip to the state in September. “Whether all of them are running for president, I can't tell you, but I am really anxious to see who does.” Haaland, a former Secretary of the Interior and the first Native American woman elected to a governorship, is ready to wield her own influence in the process as well, flexing her new power broker status . “I would love to endorse, but I'll wait and see who throws their hat in the ring,” she said. Haaland was swept into office with a historic number of fellow Democrats across the country on a mandate to deliver on affordability. It’s the “biggest issue” in New Mexico, Haaland said, adding that her priority to deliver lower costs for New Mexicans will start with expanding access to affordable health care. “Right now we're talking with some of the leaders in the legislature about health care, a public option for people in New Mexico,” she said. “Health care is a top top priority.”
articles.headline: This new early-state governor has advice for 2028 Democratic hopefuls

articles.body: Bo French, the far-right firebrand who centered his losing campaign for the Texas Railroad Commission on his anti-immigration stance, lost his membership at a Fort Worth country club, according to a letter obtained by POLITICO . The letter from River Crest Country Club, dated Nov. 10 and addressed to French, said the club’s board of directors voted to terminate French’s membership immediately “for reasons relating to the reputation and general welfare of the Club.” French said Wednesday on social media that the board asked him to resign in September due to "racist posts." He said he refused to do so, leading to an expulsion meeting. "Nothing I said in September was racist," he said in a published statement that he read to the board. The country club, founded in 1911, is the eighth to open in the state and boasts being a “who’s who” of Fort Worth. It hosts a 6,368-yard golf course that has been a training ground for top golfers, according to its website. River Crest declined to comment, citing its policy of not doing so about “past, present and prospective members” and club operations, its general manager said in an email. French, who has a history of making controversial statements on immigration issues like the H-1B visa program, made headlines in September after going viral on social media for a post he made that appeared to disparage Asian American students at the University of Texas at Austin. His remarks capitalized on the growing anti-Indian sentiment sweeping Texas and across the nation , particularly against holders of the high-skilled worker visa, a majority of whom are from India. The post quickly drew rebukes from Democrats and some Texas Republicans, who denounced it as racist. But French stood by the post . He said he was criticizing admission and hiring policies at UT, the state’s public flagship, that he claimed discriminated against Texas residents. (State law requires a majority of admitted students at the school to be residents of the state.) French lost by 677,000 votes in his bid to sit on the influential statewide body that regulates Texas’ oil and gas industry two months later amid a statewide wipeout for the GOP. He previously led the Tarrant County Republican Party and also had two unsuccessful state House bids. French did not respond to requests for comment sent to multiple email addresses associated with him. Ashley Ahn contributed reporting.
articles.headline: Bo French loses Texas country club membership

articles.body: Sen. Bernie Moreno isn’t sugarcoating things. The incoming chair of the National Republican Senatorial Committee will be in charge of defending 19 GOP seats in 2028 — and he’ll need to flip at least six more to regain control of the Senate majority. “Looking at it right now, it's absolutely a savagely brutal map,” the Ohio Republican said in an interview on Capitol Hill. After a historic midterms shellacking, Moreno is in the hot seat as he looks to navigate his chamber — and the party — through a rebuilding of its brand and its base over next two years. Republicans will likely have just 44 seats heading into 2028. They need to hold onto seats in battleground states like Wisconsin and North Carolina, while trying to flip seats held by Democratic Sens. Mark Kelly in Arizona, John Fetterman in Pennsylvania, Raphael Warnock in Georgia and Catherine Cortez Masto in Nevada. Moreno and his team have interviewed a handful of candidates over the last few days to be the next NRSC executive director, according to four people with direct knowledge of the matter, granted anonymity to discuss private conversations. Republicans expect Chris Grant, a former Moreno and Trump campaign staffer who now runs his own firm, to serve as a main outside GOP consultant for the committee. On top of the grueling map ahead, the Ohio Republican is facing the additional task of working with a lame duck president who still wields immense power over the GOP and its primaries. Then there’s the vice president, who is likely to run for president himself in the same two-year sprint. Moreno is close with both of those men. Asked how involved he expects the White House to be in GOP primaries and recruiting going forward, he replied, “We’re going to work on all of that.” It’ll be a complicated path forward. Moreno, over the past cycle has been unwilling to cast blame on President Donald Trump or Vice President JD Vance. Days before the midterm elections, he said if Republicans lost, it would be because people were “pissed off” about high gas prices. He’s unlikely to completely distance himself and the NRSC brand from the president's influence. But the party is currently undergoing a reckoning of how closely to align with the president after voters delivered an uncompromising rebuke of Trump’s economic agenda. Across the country, several battlegrounds and once-thought-to-be-safe red territory fell to Democratic hands. Trump in the 2026 cycle angered many Senate Republicans by supporting a primary challenge against Sen. John Cornyn of Texas — a move they privately say cost them north of $200 million as they tried, in vain, to save Ken Paxton’s imperiled campaign. The president also supported a primary challenge against Sen. Bill Cassidy of Louisiana, and pushed Sen. Thom Tillis to decide to retire in highly competitive North Carolina. One of the biggest challenges before Moreno and Senate Republicans after the midterms wipeout is to find candidates who can win a general election in highly competitive states, while also making it through GOP primaries where Trump will be a major factor. They’ll need to push back on the White House if the president tries, once again, to intervene — though that’s easier said than done. “There will be no patience for bad recruits this cycle,” said one senior Republican granted anonymity to discuss internal conversations, referring to the implosions of Paxton, Michael Whatley in North Carolina and other Republicans who were hand-picked by Trump. The White House referred POLITICO to Trump's post-midterms comments, where he blamed his party’s losses on the fact that he wasn’t on the ballot and said he brought several candidates "closer to victory," though they ultimately lost. Senate Majority Leader John Thune — who will be the minority leader next year — and his team plan to be heavily involved in recruitment efforts, according to two people involved in the conversations, granted anonymity to speak candidly. Their goal, one of the people said, is “to make sure we have our strongest possible candidates on the ballot in 2028.” Moreno is already trying to find a GOP recruit in his home state of Ohio to run against incoming Democratic Sen. Sherrod Brown, whose term will be up again in 2028 after he won a special election against GOP Sen. Jon Husted earlier this month. The new NRSC chair said he’s looking for “somebody who can beat the crap out of Sherrod Brown.” Husted in private conversations hasn’t completely ruled out another bid, but he’s indicated he’s unlikely to run again, according to three people with knowledge of the matter, granted anonymity to speak candidly. Ohio Republicans expect former state Sen. Kevin Coughlin to explore a potential Senate bid. And they’re watching Rep. Mike Turner (R-Ohio), who just lost his reelection. Husted did not respond to a request for comment. A Turner spokesperson said in a statement that the representative "has been approached by several people about this and is keeping all his options open.” If Vance doesn’t seek his own presidential bid, Republicans in his home state are holding a long-shot hope that he, too, might consider a return to his old job. “JD Vance would be a dream candidate,” said one Ohio Republican. You’ll also receive daily policy news and other intelligence you need to act on the day’s biggest stories.
articles.headline: ‘A savagely brutal map’: Senate GOP braces for 2028

articles.body: Nearly twice as many Americans expect a Democrat to win the presidency in 2028 than they do a Republican, a new POLITICO Poll finds . Even one in five of President Donald Trump’s own 2024 voters believe Republicans will lose the White House, a bad sign for the GOP as it struggles to recover from widespread losses this cycle and figure out its identity after spending a decade orbiting around Trump. Just 60% of Trump voters believe Republicans will keep the White House. Democratic voters are far more confident about their own party, according to the survey conducted by PF Global in the days after the midterm: Among voters who backed Kamala Harris, 87% expect Democrats to win in 2028. Beneath the unity is disagreement over what kind of nominee to pick. Pluralities of voters agree the next president should be a fighter when asked to choose from a list of qualities. But voters across the ideological spectrum also said they want other things from the country’s 48th president. While 43% of Harris voters want “a fighter,” 40% also selected “a progressive” and 34% chose “creative.” Among Trump voters, the 45% said they want to see “a conservative” elected president, surpassing the 39% who picked “a fighter.” They're also divided over what background their nominees should come from. Nearly three in 10 Trump voters say they would prefer the next president be someone who has not worked in Trump’s administration. That number rises to 46% among Trump voters who don’t identify as MAGA, whereas 82% of his loyal MAGA base would prefer the next president be someone who did work for Trump. That debate is playing out in real-time among top GOP leaders and lawmakers. More and more Hill Republicans are eyeing Secretary of State Marco Rubio for 2028, who they say is less associated with the midterm bloodbath than Vice President JD Vance. Others say the nominee should be someone entirely outside of Trump’s direct orbit. “As much as I like Rubio, and as much as I like Vance, they can't be our nominee,” said Dan McMaster, the chair of Michigan’s Shiawassee County Republican Party. “We need to get a Republican as far away from Trump as possible, and even then, I think it's going to be a battle.” “You've got to have some fresh blood in there, and you've got to have someone that has some distance from the crap that's gone on the last two years,” said one GOP strategist who worked on multiple House races last cycle and was granted anonymity to speak candidly about their own party. In a statement, Natalie Baldassarre, a spokesperson for the Republican National Committee, said the president isn’t going anywhere. "President Trump remains the unequivocal leader of our party who's cut taxes, lowered drug costs, and secured our border,” Baldassarre said. “Republicans will continue to harness his ability to energize our base and expose the Democrats' disastrous record to win in 2028." The White House also pointed POLITICO to separate polling earlier this month that shows Trump’s approval rating sits at 75% with all Republicans and jumps to 93% with those who identify as MAGA. “President Trump will never stop delivering results for the American people and he will undoubtedly go down as the most successful and consequential president in American history,” said Davis Ingle, a White House spokesperson. On election night earlier this month, Trump blamed his party’s losses on the fact that he wasn’t on the ballot, telling POLITICO by phone , “I wasn't on the ballot. If I was on the ballot, we would have won; we would have won it all very easily.” Meanwhile, Democrats have their own disagreements to figure out as they select their nominee. This cycle’s blue wave has bolstered the progressive wing of the party, which has long hoped to prove their candidates can win in purple battlegrounds, not just in safe-blue states. But the poll reveals skepticism remains — at least among moderates — over whether progressive wins in 2026 can translate to the presidential stage in 2028. The survey found a majority of progressive Democrats — 63% — want a progressive to be president, compared with just 23% of moderates who say the same. Half of progressive Democrats are convinced that being a progressive is a quality that will get their candidate elected in 2028. Moderates are less certain of that, though they’re also not as confident in their own faction: Just 37% think being a moderate is a quality that ensures the Democratic candidate wins. “Whoever's running for president has seen what's happened and also has seen the power of our movement, and so this is something that could be carried on to 2028,” said progressive New Jersey Democratic Rep.-elect Adam Hamawy, reflecting on the wins he and others enjoyed this cycle. “Despite it being the most expensive elections in history, we showed that people are able to beat out money when we come together.” And with Democrats winning Senate seats in deep-red states like Kansas and Mississippi for the first time in decades, many now argue that the entire map is in play for 2028. The poll found that 60% of Democrats think the party should focus their efforts on winning all states in the presidential election, even ones that seemed like deep Republican areas, rather than focus on holding the states where they know their supporters are. Republicans felt the same, with 56% also arguing for an “all states” approach as the party races to rebuild in territory they once thought was safe. “I have been very, very loud about the fact that the path to the presidency leads through the South,” said Democratic strategist Dallas Jones, who ran statewide Black voter engagement for Lone Star Rising PAC, the outside group that supported Texas Sen.-elect James Talarico. “But again, we don't make investments there. We're playing the same electoral map with the same swing states.”

articles.body: <p>La rivalidad entre Pedro Sánchez y Alberto Núñez Feijóo tiene mucho de personal, lamentablemente. Sus intercambios en las sesiones de control parlamentarias han dejado un terreno de humillaciones y descalificaciones difíciles de superar. No tienen comunicación personal directa como debería ser recomendable entre un presidente y un líder de la oposición. <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-11-19/sanchez-y-feijoo-ni-se-miran-porque-no-pueden-ni-verse.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-11-19/sanchez-y-feijoo-ni-se-miran-porque-no-pueden-ni-verse.html">El desprecio mutuo supura en sus miradas</a> y se refleja en toda su comunicación: desde lo que dicen a cómo lo dicen. Y sus cuerpos hablan. No se soportan y, con ello, renuncian a convencer y a entender lo que representa el adversario. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/opinion/2026-11-19/feijoo-sorprende-ante-un-sanchez-incomodo.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: <p>Una y otra vez esperamos los debates con la excitación de una ronda de penaltis, y una y otra vez los debates se encargan de aplicar hielo sobre nuestra calentura: nadie deja nunca al rival a cero, nadie da nunca un golpe triunfal, nadie se ha retirado nunca mostrando al público la simbólica cabellera del contrario. Para desatar de verdad el fervor hay que conocer el resultado final, y para conocer el resultado final hay que esperar hasta el domingo. Para más frustración, ni siquiera este domingo. Y, con el precedente de 2023 —<a href="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2023-07-10/quien-ha-sido-el-ganador-del-debate-sanchez-feijoo-de-las-elecciones-generales.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2023-07-10/quien-ha-sido-el-ganador-del-debate-sanchez-feijoo-de-las-elecciones-generales.html">Feijóo ganó el debate y Sánchez la presidencia</a>—, ya sabíamos que en diez días no hay sensación de derrota o de triunfo que no pueda aguarse. Para más inri, de este cara a cara de 2026 podemos pensar que el marcador provisional, ya que no el resultado final, indica tablas.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/opinion/2026-11-19/jessica-feijoo-vs-maricarmen-sanchez.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: <p>El presidente de los obispos españoles, Luis Javier Argüello García, buscaba el lunes ser faro para los votantes católicos y se ha convertido en polo. La palabra de moda, la polarización, ha estallado de nuevo, esta vez en la Conferencia Episcopal. Reunida para aprobar media docena de asuntos de enjundia, Argüello, que es, además, arzobispo de Valladolid, quería colar en el orden del día una “declaración” electoral, pero se ha topado con los polos que perviven en su organización, con extremos muy acusados. Lo percibió sin matices el papa Francisco cuando dijo que no vendría a España hasta que no hubiera paz entre los obispos. Fue pontífice 14 años y nunca vino.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-11-19/los-obispos-se-enzarzan-por-el-intento-de-orientar-el-voto-catolico-con-una-declaracion-oficial.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: <p>El Tribunal Constitucional ha dictaminado que los mensajes del tuitero Fonsi Loaiza en los que atribuía al “Estado policial” y a los agentes “de Madrid” la muerte de un <i>mantero </i>senegalés en el barrio de Lavapiés están amparados por la libertad de expresión. Loaiza, que publicó sus mensajes en marzo de 2018 en la red social X, cuando aún se llamaba Twitter, vivía en Barcelona, desde donde siguió los disturbios desatados en ese barrio madrileño tras la muerte del ciudadano senegalés Mame Mbaye, y escribió: “Su único delito: carecer de unos papeles. No se ha muerto solo ni es una muerte natural, es un asesinato y es culpable el Estado policial español”, decía uno de sus mensajes. “Asesinado por la policía de Madrid”, afirmaba en otro. Condenado por “injurias graves a la Policía Municipal” a una multa de 2.100 euros —y cárcel, en caso de impago—, el órgano de garantías ha estimado este miércoles el amparo de Loaiza porque la condena vulneró su derecho a la libertad de expresión. Los mensajes no deben analizarse como “información” relativa a un delito y una autoría concretos, concluye una amplia mayoría del pleno del Constitucional. Tres de los doce magistrados emitirán un voto particular en contra. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-19/el-constitucional-absuelve-al-tuitero-que-culpo-al-estado-policial-de-la-muerte-de-un-mantero-en-madrid.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>
articles.headline: El Constitucional absuelve al tuitero que culpó al “Estado policial” de la muerte de un ‘mantero’ en Madrid

articles.body: <img src="https://imagenes.elpais.com/resizer/v2/QYFUHB2MFZGFXPB7GCYOY7ZHDM.png?auth=5453e4b383eea73ee5379f604cf293cd5773b8c29785e4ed1eb2cd1b9f914f32" width="1904" height="1052" alt="El candidato socialista al 29-N, Pedro Sánchez, durante un anuncio electoral."></img><p>“El próximo 29 de noviembre”, interrumpe Pedro Sánchez con una sonrisa a cámara para botar tres veces la pelota de baloncesto, “todo el mundo votando”. <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-11-17/yo-te-voy-a-votar-adrian-el-cocinero-valenciano-que-compuso-la-cancion-viral-de-sanchez-en-tiktok-y-no-recibio-respuesta-del-psoe.html" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer" title="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-11-17/yo-te-voy-a-votar-adrian-el-cocinero-valenciano-que-compuso-la-cancion-viral-de-sanchez-en-tiktok-y-no-recibio-respuesta-del-psoe.html">El nuevo vídeo de campaña del PSOE</a> para redes sociales está dando que hablar: desde la camiseta del Estudiantes, equipo en el que el presidente del Gobierno jugó de joven, hasta el grito de la cantante Bad Gyal que cierra el anuncio electoral, un segundo guiño al juego de palabras: “Todo el mundo botando”. Todo ello para presentar un bono para fomentar el deporte de 200 euros al año destinado a los jóvenes de entre 18 y 25 años como parte de su programa electoral, y pedir el voto. Una propuesta que el PP no ha tardado en criticar, calificándola de “paguita”. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-11-19/el-29-de-noviembre-todo-el-mundo-votando-sanchez-llama-al-voto-joven-a-la-vez-que-promete-un-bono-para-el-deporte-de-200-euros.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: <p>Casi cuatro meses después de la entrada masiva de migrantes a Ceuta, las redes encargadas del tráfico de personas <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-21/las-mafias-cobran-9000-euros-a-los-migrantes-de-la-entrada-masiva-en-ceuta-por-llevarlos-en-lancha-a-la-peninsula.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-21/las-mafias-cobran-9000-euros-a-los-migrantes-de-la-entrada-masiva-en-ceuta-por-llevarlos-en-lancha-a-la-peninsula.html">siguen haciendo grandes esfuerzos para sortear el control policial </a>y llevar de forma ilegal a la Península a las personas que quedaron varadas en la ciudad autónoma. La última operación de la Policía, difundida este jueves, recoge cómo estos grupos delictivos sitúan a personas de su confianza en playas de la costa gaditana para recibir las embarcaciones en las que viajan los migrantes, la gestión de pagos de hasta 8.000 euros por estos trayectos que se abonan desde Marruecos y las precarias condiciones en las que los migrantes se esconden en Ceuta hasta que llega el momento de embarcarse, sufriendo encierros e incluso amenazas con armas de fuego. La operación se ha saldado con cuatro detenciones, aunque permanece abierta y no se descartan nuevas actuaciones. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-19/pagos-desde-marruecos-y-esperas-en-las-playas-de-la-linea-asi-funcionaba-la-ultima-red-de-pase-de-migrantes-de-ceuta.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>
articles.headline: Pagos desde Marruecos y esperas en las playas de La Línea, así funcionaba la última red de pase de migrantes de Ceuta

articles.body: <p>Ada Colau (Barcelona, 52 años) se presenta a las generales del 29-N para cambiar radicalmente las políticas públicas de vivienda en España. Motivada por el clamor en la calle que <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-05/sanchez-adelanta-las-elecciones-al-29-de-noviembre-necesitamos-una-mayoria-progresista-mucho-mas-amplia.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-05/sanchez-adelanta-las-elecciones-al-29-de-noviembre-necesitamos-una-mayoria-progresista-mucho-mas-amplia.html">precipitó las elecciones</a> y la aprobación del decreto para prorrogar los alquileres que su espacio político peleó más de un año en el Ejecutivo con el PSOE, la <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-10-12/el-frente-amplio-propone-a-ada-colau-como-candidata-a-la-presidencia-y-deja-abierta-la-integracion-de-podemos.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-10-12/el-frente-amplio-propone-a-ada-colau-como-candidata-a-la-presidencia-y-deja-abierta-la-integracion-de-podemos.html">candidata de Frente Amplio (FA)</a>, activista antidesahucios durante décadas y alcaldesa de Barcelona de 2015 a 2023, se esfuerza en combatir los llamamientos al voto útil de Sánchez, que amenaza con menguar su representación en el próximo Congreso. articles.body: El Barça havia tingut un clar toc d’atenció: dos empats consecutius , contra l’Arsenal a la Champions i davant el Depor a la Lliga. Una casuística que no es donava des del febrer del 2019, el fet que el Barça encadenés dos partits sense guanyar. Per posar-hi remei, tenien un escenari ideal: el Johan Cruyff , fortí de les blaugrana, en un duel contra un Servette suís que només havia guanyat un partit a la Fase Lliga de la Champions i que arribava com l’equip més golejat. Tot i que encara li falta recuperar finor i més fluïdesa en el joc, el Barça ha tornat al camí de la victòria amb el que més li agrada: una golejada a la màxima competició europea. 6-0 amb hat-trick de Pina i gols d’Aitana , Brugts i Graham . Amb aquesta victòria, l’equip de Pere Romeu certifica matemàticament la classificació per als quarts de final de la Champions i se situa primer de grup quan queda només una jornada de la lligueta prèvia. Sumen 13 punts, els mateixos que l’ Olympique de Lió , que també ha guanyat contra l’Arsenal (2-0), però a qui superen per diferència de gols. L’objectiu entre cella i cella la final a Varsòvia el maig del 2027. Una Claudia Pina estel·lar: hat-trick i assistència contra el Servette El Barça ha necessitat una estona per sentir-se còmode i trobar porteria. Després de 18 minuts en què Pere Romeu es resignava i donava indicacions constants, Aitana Bonmatí amb un toc suau i subtil ha fet el primer a assistència d’una Clàudia Pina clau en aquest triomf. Primer gol d’Aitana a la Champions en aquest curs, que està tornant a poc a poc després de la lesió i els dolors que arrossegava al turmell. Un cop ha arribat el primer, han començat a caure la resta de gols. Al minut 26, Pina ha fet el segon, en aquest cas gràcies a una assistència d’Aitana. Intercanvi de papers. Passada la mitja hora de joc, Esmee Brugts ha estat la protagonista del 3-0 després d’una gran centrada de Graham Hansen. A la represa, i quan havien passat 15 minuts de joc, penal a favor del Barça per una falta sobre Brugts i Graham que no ha fallat des dels onze metres. La golejada l’ha tancat la que s’ha convertit en la màxima golejadora de la Champions -empatada a 7 dianes amb Katoto-. Clàudia Pina, exhibint un gran nivell, ha fet dos gols més a les acaballes per tancar el 6-0 definitiu. articles.body: Tot just quan arriba l’equador de la campanya electoral , aquest dijous comença la ronda de debats televisats amb el cara a cara entre Pedro Sánchez i Alberto Núñez Feijóo . Uns debats on tot s’analitza: els missatges dels candidats, les picabaralles, la posada en escena, la indumentària i la comunicació no verbal. Un escrutini que acaba definint qui guanya i qui perd els debats i que pot ajudar a definir el vot dels electors indecisos . El consultor de comunicació política i xarxes socials, Xavier Tomàs , ha explicat al bàsics de betevé que, per preparar-se un debat cara a cara, els candidats ho fan “com es fa al futbol , que s’estudia el rival”. Segons Tomàs, es fixen en “quins tics té o quins hàbits té per poder-los contestar”. A banda d’això, també pot entrar en joc el que ha denominat com a “ factor X “. Es tracta d’alguna sorpresa que es puguin treure de la màniga “en forma de proposta , de crítica o d’argument “. Segons les dades de Xavier Tomàs, gairebé un 13 % dels espectadors del cara a cara del 2023 van reconèixer que canviarien el sentit del vot després d’haver vist el debat. El pes de Catalunya i l’habitatge escalfen el 1r debat de candidats catalans a les generals del 29-N Marina Segura i Vidal Roger Torres i Liñán 4 minuts de lectura Els nous formats entren en joc durant la campanya La gran novetat de la campanya d’enguany ha estat l’aparició dels candidats en espais que no s’havien vist fins ara. És el cas de la ronda d’entrevistes al pòdcast de Jordi Wild o les que han fet en un programa humorístic com ‘ La Revuelta ‘. “Comencen a veure que és igual d’important dedicar temps a un míting , a un barri, a un mercat o a un podcàster”, ha resumit Tomàs. A banda, l’expert en comunicació política ha explicat que, en unes eleccions on es preveu una participació molt alta , “encara és més important buscar gent no polititzada “. A més, la convocatòria anticipada i el poc temps que ha passat fins l’arribada de la campanya ha provocat que hagin d’escollir molt bé on volien anar per ser entrevistats. articles.body: Primera setmana de campanya de les eleccions generals del 2026 , pràcticament al sac. El sisè dia de la cursa cap al 29-N ha estat marcat per una entrevista a l’expresident Carles Puigdemont a El Mundo en què ha afirmat que “va aprofitar l ‘ambició desmesurada de Sánchez per derrotar Espanya”, en referència a la llei d’amnistia per als polítics independentistes encausats. Una entrevista que ha generat molta polèmica a tots els espais polítics. A banda, també ha estat protagonista de la jornada la presidenta de la Comunitat de Madrid, la popular Isabel Díaz Ayuso , que ha visitat Sarrià – Sant Gervasi acompanyada del cap de llista del PP a Barcelona, Xavier García Albiol. És la primera vegada que Ayuso trepitja Barcelona —i Catalunya— durant aquesta campanya. Per saber-ne més Tota la informació de les eleccions generals del 29-N Consulta totes les dades i notícies disponibles Hereu (PSC): “Allà Junts amb la seva irresponsabilitat” Pel candidat socialista per Barcelona, Jordi Hereu , l’entrevista de Puigdemont a El Mundo demostra que “l’ agenda de retrobament ” impulsada pel govern de Pedro Sánchez per tancar el conflicte Catalunya-Espanya després del procés “ha estat un gran èxit “. Ara bé, el ministre ha qüestionat la tria que l’expresident ha fet del mitjà de comunicació: “ Junts ja no està al centre , ha pres partit. Ja ho sabíem, però ara se n’ha assabentat tothom. Allà ells amb la seva irresponsabilitat “, ha dit. En tot cas, Hereu ha assegurat que aquest “ gran error estratègic ” dels juntaires afavoreix electoralment el PSC. “Ens obre molt més espai. Tota la gent que posa Catalunya per sobre de tot també s’ha d’unir a aquesta àmplia convocatòria que fem”, ha demanat. Tot plegat ho ha dit des de l’acte Barcelona Tribuna, des d’on també ha avisat que ara comença “l’ operació cap a la victòria ” dels socialistes. Jordi Hereu en un acte a Barcelona Tribuna. Foto: ACN Urtasun (Front Ampli): “Puigdemont fa el joc a la dreta mediàtica que l’ha perseguit” En una roda de premsa a l’agència EFE, el número dos de Front Ampli a Barcelona, Ernest Urtasun , també ha criticat durament l’entrevista de Puigdemont: “M’ha sobtat que ara faci el joc a tota la dreta política i mediàtica de Madrid que l’ha perseguit durant tants anys”, ha dit, i ha afegit: “També he de dir que és on s’està situant Junts, en aquesta posició d’equidistància”. En la mateixa atenció als mitjans, Urtasun ha proposat crear un hub del videojoc a Catalunya per donar un “impuls” al sector i “convertir-nos en un pol punter a escala internacional i europea”. El hub , ha dit, hauria de tenir el suport de la Generalitat, els ajuntaments, el Ministeri de Cultura i el mateix sector. Ernest Urtasun en una roda de premsa a l’agència EFE. Foto: ACN Ayuso (PP) visita Sarrià – Sant Gervasi Un altre plat fort d’aquest sisè dia de campanya ha estat la visita de la madrilenya Ayuso a Sarrià – Sant Gervasi. Ha acompanyat el líder municipal del PP, Daniel Sirera , i el cap de llista popular a Barcelona, Xavier García Albiol . Han fet un acte a la plaça d’Artós, que en els últims anys s’ha convertit en punt de trobada de l’ unionisme . Des d’allà, i rodejada de mig miler llarg de simpatitzants, Ayuso ha acusat Sánchez de voler carregar-se l’estat de dret i ha alertat què està en joc en aquestes generals: “El 29-N Espanya ha de decidir si se suïcida “. Albiol, al seu torn, ha preguntat als simpatitzants (en referència a les seves propostes contra l’ocupació il·legal): “Qui m’ajudarà a desocupar Pedro Sánchez de La Moncloa ?”. En paral·lel, s’ha desfet en elogis a Ayuso, de qui ha dit que ha convertit Madrid “en la capital de la llibertat”. Isabel Díaz Ayuso en un acte de campanya a Sarrià – Sant Gervasi Rufián (ERC), a Junts: “Respectin la institució de la presidència” El candidat republicà, Gabriel Rufián , ha carregat també contra l’expresident Carles Puigdemont i el seu partit per l’entrevista a El Mundo , a qui ha demanat que “ respectin una institució tan important com és la de la presidència de la Generalitat “. A més, ha defensat que va ser ERC “qui va treure gent de la presó, entre crits de botiflers i traïdors “. En el primer debat de candidats catalans que aquest dijous han fet RAC1 i La Vanguardia , Rufián també ha assenyalat el fet que el periodista que ha entrevistat Puigdemont és el mateix que va acusar l’exalcalde de Barcelona Xavier Trias de tenir comptes bancaris fraudulents a Suïssa en la campanya electoral de les municipals del 2015. En una roda de premsa a l’ACN, Rufián ha afegit que “l’únic que desitja la dreta catalana és que després del 29-N iniciï un període de reflexió i torni a la racionalitat”. Gabriel Rufián en una roda de premsa a l’ACN. Foto: ACN Turull (Junts) defensa Puigdemont El secretari general de Junts, Jordi Turull , ha entrat en la campanya de Míriam Nogueras per defensar Puigdemont i ha dit que considera l’entrevista “una doble victòria ” perquè suposa “derrotar l’Estat i la toga nostra “. “Si algú ha de donar explicacions són aquells que van intentar-ho tot per combatre’ns i que ara ens van darrere per fer una entrevista”, ha dit. A més, ha afegit que considera “molt bo que el president s’expliqui davant del públic que voldria fer-nos desaparèixer “. En la mateixa atenció a mitjans, Turull ha reivindicat que el seu partit és el “ vot més útil contra l’extrema dreta” i l’únic que garantirà que Catalunya “ condicioni totes les decisions d’Espanya en benefici dels catalans i les catalanes”. En la mateixa línia s’ha expressat la candidata del partit, Míriam Nogueras , al debat de candidats, unes hores abans. Míriam Nogueras al debat de RAC1 i La Vanguardia Aizcorbe (Vox): “Junts només ha lluitat per l’amnistia, no pels catalans” Pel cap de llista de Vox a Barcelona, Juan José Aizcorbe , l’entrevista de l’expresident evidencia que “Junts i Puigdemont només han lluitat per l’amnistia” i que no ho han fet, en canvi, “ni pels catalans, ni pel seu benestar, ni pel seu finançament, ni per Rodalies”. “I no tan sols això, sinó que Junts i el PSOE han fet pinya aquesta legislatura, han sigut el mateix”, ha sentenciat. articles.body: Les nits més fredes de l’hiven a les zones baixes, en valls i fondalades , acostumen a registrar-se després de l’entrada d’una massa d’aire fred, quan encalma el vent. Per contra, si després d’una entrada freda entra el vent del nord o del nord-oest , la tempertura mínima nocturna serà més alta però, per contra, notarem probablement una major sensació de fredor. Temperatura mínima de dijous, 23 de novembre del 2023. Font CMI També et pot interessar Per què quan fa vent no baixa tant la temperatura però notem més el fred? Manel Cascante Torrella 3 minuts de lectura Si s’encalma el vent i el cel es manté serè baixa més la temperatura Quan arriba una massa d’aire més fred en altura , la temperatura baixa sobtadament a les cotes mitjanes i altes de les muntanyes. Mentre es manté l’entrada freda, la temperatura és clarament més baixa a major altura. Les temperatures més baixes es registren, per tant, als cims de les muntanyes i les més suaus a les zones més baixes de l’interior i a la costa. Tan bon punt com es talla l’entrada freda, l’aire fred —més dens i pesat— acostuma a anar-se dipositant cap a les zones més baixes i enclotades. Aquest fet sol anar vinculat a l’arribada de l’anticicló, que afavoreix el fenomen de la subsidència , és a dir, el predomini de moviments descendents que faciliten aquesta acumulació d’aire fred cap a les parts més baixes de les valls i fondalades . Si a més el cel es manté serè i el vent s’encalma, la superfície terrestre perd calor per radiació en hores nocturnes. Tot plegat incrementa l’acumulació d’aire fred a les zones més baixes. La temperatura mínima, en aquest context, es produeix a les valls, no a les muntanyes, on l’ambient sol ser força més càlid a causa del fenomen de la inversió tèrmica. El vent barreja la columna d’aire fent que la temperatura s’acabi uniformitzant . En aquest context la temperatura acabarà sent més suau a les cotes més baixes i més alta a major altura. La temperatura acostuma a disminuir a la troposfera de mitjana 0,65 ºC cada 100 metres , tot i que aquest descens del termòmetre en funció de l’altura no sempre és igual , varia en funció de la situació meteorològica en la qual ens trobem i es veu condicionat, en alguns casos, per la presència de relleu ( efecte fogony ). També et pot interessar Per què el vent de ponent arriba sec i reescalfat a Barcelona? Manel Cascante Torrella Marcos Amores Sánchez Oriol Rodríguez Ballester 1 minut de lectura El vent dificulta el refredament nocturn però accentua la sensació de fred És ben sabut que el vent provoca una sensació de fred major que la que marca el termòmetre . El motiu és que el v ent accentua la pèrdua de calor del cos humà perquè retira i renova la capa d’aire protectora que se situa damunt la pell. A l’estiu, a tall d’exemple, usem el  ventilador per refrescar-nos perquè el que fa és renovar constantment la capa d’humitat que hi ha damunt de la pell i afavoreix, d’aquesta manera, l’evaporació de la suor. El resultat és que  el nostre cos es refrigera i fa que assolim el confort tèrmic . L ‘índex de fredor serveix per aproximar el ritme de pèrdua de calor que pot patir el cos humà com a conseqüència de l’efecte combinat de les baixes temperatures amb el vent. Aquest índex no és estrictament una temperatura, sinó una quantitat sense unitats que permet quantificar l’efecte addicional de refredament que aporta el vent damunt la pell humana. L’índex de fredor s’empra sobretot quan la temperatura és inferior als 0 ºC i és de gran utilitat per als muntanyencs. articles.body: (ACN/Redacció) El Departament de Justícia admet que hi ha una plaga de ratolins en una part de la seu del Tribunal Superior de Justícia de Catalunya (TSJC). L’aparició de rosegadors es dona concretament a les dependències dels Mossos d’Esquadra destinats a l’edifici del tribunal. En un comunicat, el sindicat de Mossos SAP-ME Fepol ha denunciat la manca de salubritat i assegura que la calor, la pluja i la humitat afavoreixen la proliferació de paneroles, mosquits, mosques, rates i ratolins. Segons Justícia, des del setembre s’estan fent actuacions de manera continuada per controlar la plaga. En aquest aspecte, el sindicat ha indicat que la situació afecta el menjador, els vestidors , situats al subsol i, fins i tot, l’interior dels armariets personals. Per tot això, critiquen que aquestes condicions afecten la higiene del personal i dificulten la prestació del servei ordinari. Paral·lelament, Justícia ha demanat la col·laboració de l’Ajuntament de Barcelona perquè pugui intervenir també en l’àmbit del subsol. articles.body: La cantant Rosalía ha fet una aparició sorpresa aquest dijous al vespre al centre de Barcelona. L’artista ha participat en una campanya publicitària de la marca New Balance al Convent dels Àngels, a la plaça dels Àngels, al Raval. Una estona abans d’arribar, ha començat a córrer per les xarxes socials missatges que apuntaven que Rosalía participaria en un esdeveniment d’aquesta marca esportiva. Els entorns del MACBA s’han omplert d’una allau de curiosos i fans de la cantant , que han volgut comprovar en persona si el rumor era cert i si tenien la sort de veure-la. A mitja tarda, l’artista ha aparegut i ha repartit vambes entre els qui s’aplegaven allà. articles.body: A l’hivern és habitual que els habitants de pobles i ciutats de l’entorn metropolità de Barcelona hagin de destinar uns minuts del preuat temps matinal per treure el gel del vidre del cotxe. Això, només si no van preveure deixar-hi un cartró el vespre anterior. Aquest hidrometeor és un clàssic de les nits serenes dels mesos freds als Pirineus i l’interior del país , però és menys freqüent a prop del mar i, sobretot, a l’interior de grans ciutats litorals com Barcelona , on l’efecte illa de calor dificulta el descens del termòmetre nocturn. A Barcelona pot observar-se sovint als barris pròxims al Besòs, especialment cap a Torre Baró, el nus de la Trinitat i el Bon Pastor. També és habitual en nits fredes i serenes a les zones fondes de Collserola, sobretot al cantó nord de la serra. També et pot interessar L’illa de calor a Barcelona: 6 ºC de diferència entre el centre i la perifèria Marcos Amores Sánchez 4 minuts de lectura Per què es gela el vidre o el terra si la temperatura és positiva? Molts conductors deuen haver observat que, en algunes ocasions, malgrat haver hagut de rascar el vidre, en mirar la temperatura exterior que indicava el seu cotxe era lleugerament positiva, de fins a tres o quatre graus sobre zero, en alguns casos. El cert és que la temperatura sol variar força en funció de la distància del terra o d’una superfície quan el cel és serè, especialment en un context d’inversió tèrmica. És a dir, en nits serenes i sense vent, en un context anticiclònic, la temperatura pot baixar molt més arran de terra que no pas a 1 o 1,5 m del sòl , l’altura dels sensors meteorològics oficials, per exemple. Inversió tèrmica molt marcada a Sant Fost de Campsentelles . Sortir de casa a Mas Corts a 6°C i arribar a Can Coromines a -1,6°C @eltempsTV3 @alcantara_alb @gemmapuigf @SoniaPapell @SergiLoras @eltemps_rtve @ARAmeteo @btveltemps @MeteoMauri @meteocat @AEMET_Cat pic.twitter.com/QycLvYunbK — MeteoSantFost (@MeteoSantFost) December 17, 2024 Per entendre el perquè d’aquesta diferència tèrmica en funció de l’altura convé recordar abans que els rajos solars creuen la troposfera de dia sense elevar significativament la seva temperatura . Una part d’aquesta energia solar d’ona curta l’absorbeix directament la superfície terrestre —la qual s’escalfa— i l’allibera a posteriori en forma de calor (radiació d’ona llarga). Aquesta calor emesa per la superfície del sol i dels objectes escalfa les capes d’aire més pròximes a terra i fa que la temperatura, en dies assolellats, sigui més alta com més a prop de terra. En nits serenes i mancades de vent (típiques de situacions anticiclòniques) s’inverteix aquest procés: el terra perd calor de terra per irradiació . Això fa que el sòl i la superfície dels objectes (el vidre o el capó del cotxe) perdin calor amb celeritat. El resultat és que la temperatura és clarament més baixa a tocar de terra o uns pocs centímetres per damunt que a l’altura on se situen els sensors i termòmetres dels observatoris meteorològics (o del cotxe). Com més baixa sigui la humitat ambiental més alta serà aquesta diferència tèrmica. També et pot interessar Gelada, glaçada, gebrada o rosada? T’expliquem les diferències La gelada es forma quan hi ha cel ras i poc vent, mentre que en la gebrada el cel és emboirat Gel damunt del vidre o del capó del cotxe Si la temperatura del terra baixa dels 0 ºC i hi ha prou humitat ambiental (vapor d’aigua) es formen cristalls de gel damunt la superfície del sòl o a l’herba (gelada) . Això també passa damunt del vidre del cotxe o el metall del capó , que es refreden més que l’aire pròxim situat a una altura similar i poden quedar gelats. El cel serè i la manca de vent permeten la pèrdua de més calor per part del sòl que no pas si el cel està cobert , ja que els núvols actuen de tapadora i retornen part de l’energia novament cap a la superfície. Quan el cel és cobert o fa vent, la diferència sol atenuar-se o desapareix. A l’interior de Barcelona és difícil observar aquest fenomen, molt més habitual als barris pròxims al Besòs o Collserola. articles.body: (ACN/Redacció) El sindicat majoritari dels maquinistes SEMAF ha convocat dilluns vinent una altra vaga de 24 hores a Rodalies . Per a aquesta aturada, la Generalitat ha fixat uns serveis mínims del 66 % dels trens en hora punta (de les 6 h fins a les 9.30 h i de les 17 h fins a les 20.30 h) i del 33 % dels combois per la resta d’hores de la jornada. Per garantir l’estricte compliment d’aquests serveis essencials, Renfe està contactant des de dimecres amb els maquinistes que hauran de prestar la circulació obligatòria dels trens durant la vaga, segons ha avançat Catalunya Ràdio i ha confirmat l’ACN. Així l’operadora ha enviat un correu electrònic i està entregant des d’aquest dijous les cartes a mà amb els detalls dels serveis mínims als treballadors assignats per conduir els combois . Amb això, Renfe vol evitar l’incompliment dels serveis mínims que s’han repetit en les darreres aturades dels maquinistes: el 10 de novembre, l’11 de novembre coincidint amb la vaga general i el 17 de novembre. També et pot interessar Jornada de vaga a Renfe: Rodalies avisa que s’incompleixen compleixen els serveis mínims Marta Casals Torres 3 minuts de lectura Seguint el procediment habitual L’empresa ferroviària ha detallat que fins ara també feia enviaments electrònics i a mà i que està seguint el procediment habitual de notificacions en cas d’aturada. Per la seva banda, SEMAF manté la vaga després de desmarcar-se de l’acord tancat entre el Ministeri de Transports i diverses organitzacions sindicals com CCOO, UGT o el Sindicat de Circulació Ferroviari, que agrupa els controladors. SEMAF veu insuficient la proposta i argumenta que part de les mesures promeses encara estan pendents d’aprovar-se i d’efectuar la tramitació corresponent. A més, el sindicat ha anunciat que està estudiant convocar més mobilitzacions.
